citation: Asghari SH, Wong A, Comfort P, Mirghani SJ, Sharifian S, Ghaderi M. (2025). Comparing the impact of hip thrust versus squat training on lower limb performance in sub-elite athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sports biomechanics.
intervention: squat (SQ) training vs hip thrust (HT) training
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis compared squat and hip thrust training effects on lower-body athletic performance in sub-elite athletes. Squat training significantly improved vertical jump height with a medium effect size in the 12-16 session subgroup, while neither exercise significantly improved horizontal jump distance, sprint performance, or change-of-direction ability.
key_findings: SQ training significantly improved vertical jump height (VJH) and was superior to HT training.
Neither SQ nor HT training had a significant impact on horizontal jump distance (HJD), short sprint time (SST), short sprint performance (SSP), or change of direction (COD) performance.
In the 12 to 16 sessions subgroup, SQ training significantly improved VJH showing a medium effect size.
In other subgroups, neither SQ nor HT exercises produced significant improvements in HJD, SSP, SST, or COD performance.
No conclusive preference can be made between SQ and HT for enhancing HJD, SSP, and SST markers.
limitations: The abstract notes the need for higher-quality studies to better elucidate effects, suggesting risk of bias and heterogeneity in included studies. Population limited to sub-elite athletes, limiting generalizability to elite or recreational populations.
